# Distinct from a re-home: this records keyed assertions DELETED outright because what

column1: # The 7 work-024 delivery-002 rows were relative to the pre-work-024 merge-base and are
# already absorbed into master, so they are NOT seeded here. Later rows record task-owned
# removals after the relevant delivery has committed.

column4: Six individually keyed existence assertions (five tool artifacts plus CLI) were subsumed by the exact artifact-set equality assertion, which checks every expected filename and rejects extras in one check; RL01 drops from 8 assertions to 2 without losing artifact-name coverage.

The 15 retired per-tool layout checks assumed profile-wide roots and root files that task-007 removes from the artifact contract. RL03 now checks every archive member against each tool descriptor plus its <root>/agents tree and excludes shared paths; RL02 retains six shared-payload assertions for the new layout, dropping from 21 to 6.

The 20 internal READMEs were deleted (FR-7), so canonical/skills/aid-monitor/README.md no longer exists and an existence assert on it cannot pass. Nothing is lost: the file was internal, installed into no tree, and resolved by no instruction.

Asserted the BUG -> /aid-fix routing in the deleted README. The same routing is still asserted against SHIPPING files by DMR03a (aid-monitor/SKILL.md) and DMR01a/DMR02a (references/state-route.md), so this was a duplicate of live coverage, not coverage itself.

Asserted the Change Request -> /aid-triage routing in the deleted README. Still asserted against shipping files by DMR03b (SKILL.md) and DMR01b/DMR02b (state-route.md), so the deletion de-duplicated rather than reduced.

One of the CANONICAL_BODIES sample paths was aid/templates/delivery-blueprint-template.md, deleted when BLUEPRINT.md was retired (the delivery definition now lives in the delivery's own PLAN.md stanza). Keyed T20, NOT T13: the labels are path-normalised to <PATH>, so the array's entries collapse onto per-index keys and only the last one disappeared when the list shortened. An earlier version of this row named T13, which is still emitted -- it excused a removal that had not happened while leaving the real one un-excused. The property asserted (a canonical body with no tool-root references renders byte-identically across install trees) is unchanged and still sampled by the remaining entries.

The dogfood byte-identity suite emits ONE assertion per generator-owned file, so its count tracks how many files the generator owns. This work retired canonical templates -- delivery-blueprint-template.md with BLUEPRINT.md, and delivery-plans/flattened-plan-template.md with the Lite path's PLAN.md -- so there is one fewer file to compare per tree and the count drops accordingly. Nothing stopped being CHECKED: every file that still exists is still compared in both directions, and the suite's own ORPHAN and MUT-CTRL legs (which assert there are no undocumented extra files, and that the comparison can still detect a mutation) both pass. A reduction here is the expected arithmetic of deleting a template, not lost coverage -- which is why it belongs in this file rather than in a re-home: there is no new key to point at.

column2: T28 throwaway repo absent from real HOME registry
column4: The rewritten suite still pins HOME and verifies no new .aid directory escaped; registry-path coverage is superseded by all per-operation AID_HOME pinning and the explicit HOME canary.

WS09 emits one assertion pair per template in its loop, and the loop included delivery-blueprint-template.md, which is retired. Those 2 assertions were not testing anything: the body is `grep -qE ... "$tmpl" 2>/dev/null`, which on a MISSING file returns non-zero, fires the else branch, and PASSES -- so they had been reporting success about a file that did not exist. Removing a vacuous pass reduces the count without reducing coverage. The loop now guards existence first, so a future retired template FAILS here rather than silently repeating this.
Removed the obsolete per-profile root-context existence checks; profiles now intentionally contain no root-context files.
Removed the obsolete cross-profile root-context byte-identity check; shared canonical rules are now distributed by the CLI.
Removed hard-coded-root checks for deleted profile root-context files; shared canonical rules now use tool-neutral runtime paths.

The dogfood profile is no longer one of the generated profiles; profile generation now writes five profile directories containing agents and aid-tool.conf, while root dogfood resync is owned by task-027.

The dogfood mirror-deletion probe was retired with profile runtime-tree generation; each of the five remaining profile probes now confirms generated skills, runtime trees, and JSONL manifests are absent.
The ten profile-README count assertions were removed because generated profile README files are retired; current inventory counts remain checked against the root README and docs/ surfaces.
